references.text: The command to love the Lord your God is the central command in the Torah, which is also emphasized here
Walking in the ways of the Lord and keeping His commands is a recurring theme in Deuteronomy
The same exhortation to love the Lord, walk in His ways, and keep His commands and statutes
The promise of blessing in the land is tied to obedience to the commands and love for the Lord
The blessings that follow from keeping the Lord's commands and walking in His ways
The Lord will circumcise the heart so that the people may love Him with all their heart and live
The one who keeps the Lord's statutes and commands shall live by them
Ezekiel repeats the promise of life through keeping the Lord's laws and statutes
Jesus confirms that the greatest command is to love the Lord your God
Paul quotes the principle that the one who does the works of the law shall live by them
Paul refers to the principle that the one who does the commands shall live by them
Love for God is shown by keeping His commands, and His commands are not burdensome
